picks.name: modern-web-guidance-src
picks.desc: Keep your coding agent up to date with the latest web best practices
picks.readme:
# Modern Web Guidance (Source) This repo is the source repository for [GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance) and includes the code and documentation for authoring, calibrating, and evaluating its contents. [**Modern Web Guidance**](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance) is a set of skills that embed web platform expertise, best practices, and browser compatibility data directly into your coding agents. It helps to steer your coding agents away from legacy patterns, and instead toward solutions that harness the power and capabilities of the modern web platform. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) and [GOVERNANCE.md](./GOVERNANCE.md) for how we work on the project and orientation of the codebase. --- *Stewarded by the Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, and MDN teams, alongside the web development community.* [Documentation](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance) · [Eval Dashboard](https://googlechrome.github.io/modern-web-guidance-src/) · [Source Code](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src) · [Report an Issue](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src/issues) ## Quickstart ```shell npx modern-web-guidance@latest install ``` This command runs an interactive wizard to install Modern Web Guidance. See [Alternative Installation Methods](#-alternative-installation-methods) below. #### Try it out (without installing) ```shell # Search for relevant guides npx modern-web-guidance@latest search "animate a dialog modal backdrop" # Retrieve a guide by ID npx modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "animate-to-from-top-layer" # Scan a codebase for legacy patterns to modernize npx modern-web-guidance@latest legacy-scan . ``` ## Why? Coding agents often default to older patterns because LLM training data contains vast amounts of legacy code. This often leads them to generate bloated JavaScript for tasks that now have native, high-performance web platform solutions. Even if a model knows an API exists, it often lacks the density of real-world, modern implementation patterns required for production-ready code. **Modern Web Guidance bridges this gap.** Our skill's CLI returns targeted, expert-curated guidelines directly into your agent's context window, focusing on: * **Modern Browser APIs**: Helping models correctly structure APIs they frequently misuse. * **Performance & Accessibility**: Preferring platform-level APIs that can be optimized by the browser and include built-in accessibility affordances. * **Responsible Fallbacks**: Guiding models to use sensible, lightweight fallbacks instead of heavy polyfills or legacy libraries. ## What's Included? We cover the past several years of the web platform's new features, all the way up to the cutting edge. The guides are **designed to be token-efficient**; we run evals enabling us to prune lowest-common-denominator content that models already know. ### Core Disciplines

🎨 User Experience

Smooth visual states (View Transitions, entry/exit animations, parallax scroll, CSS scrollbar-color).

picks.name: unslop
picks.desc: A Claude skill that turns vibecoded, AI-looking UI into a designed interface
picks.readme:
# unslop

Created by Damir Sokolovsky ([@heydamir](https://x.com/heydamir)), who started the [Unslopping series](https://x.com/heydamir/status/2115063463063998736) on X.

![A vibecoded dashboard unslopping itself, frame by frame](skills/unslop/references/refs/story-dashboard-frames.webp)

unslop is a skill for Claude Code, Codex and Google Antigravity that turns vibecoded, AI-looking UI into a designed interface with its own character. It finds the slop first, the purple gradients, glows, emoji labels, shouty copy and uneven spacing, then sets a direction from your product and fixes the screen pass by pass like a designer doing a redline review. It works in whatever your screen is built with, like Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte, Tailwind or plain HTML and CSS, on dashboards, apps and landing pages, and even on a live site when all you have is a link.

## Install

For Claude Code, copy the skill into your skills folder.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.claude/skills/
```

For a single project, copy it into `.claude/skills/` inside that project instead.

For Codex, ask it to install the skill straight from this repo.

```
$skill-installer install https://github.com/heydamir/unslop/tree/main/skills/unslop
```

Or copy it by hand into `~/.agents/skills/`, or into `.agents/skills/` inside a single project.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.agents/skills/
```

For Google Antigravity, copy the skill into your skills folder.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.gemini/antigravity/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.gemini/antigravity/skills/
```

For a single project, copy it into `.agents/skills/` inside that project instead.

To snapshot a live site or create a story video, install Playwright and its Chromium browser from the project directory where you run the skill:

```bash
npm install -D playwright
npx playwright install chromium
```

Story videos also require ffmpeg installed and available on your PATH.

## Use

In Claude Code, type `/unslop` with what you want. In Codex, type `$unslop` the same way. Or just ask in your own words and the agent picks the skill up by itself.

```
/unslop this dashboard
/unslop the hero of https://example.com
/unslop my landing page and make the story video so I can post it
```

It audits the screen and proposes a direction before it edits anything, so you can steer it early. If the screen is already good, it tells you so and suggests a few small refinements instead of redesigning it.

## What it does

- **Audit.** Lists every sign of slop with where it lives.
- **Direction.** Character, world, the one or two moments that carry the color, and a signature detail, all taken from your product.
- **Passes.** Spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals and motion, in that order.
- **Visuals.** Shows your product instead of a glossy blob. When a hero needs a scene or an object, it can generate one through an image service like fal, Replicate, OpenAI images or Higgsfield. If none is connected, it offers to connect one as an MCP server, and it shows the prompt and asks before every paid generation. Dashboards and apps rarely need one.
- **Story video.** A square video under 10 seconds of your screen unslopping itself, ready to post. It needs Playwright and ffmpeg.

Try it on the two vibecoded screens in [examples](examples).

## Hire the unslopper

Would rather have a designer do it? Damir unslops one key screen in 3 days, built in your stack, at [heydamir.design/unslop](https://heydamir.design/unslop).

## License

[CC BY 4.0](LICENSE). Use it, change it and share it, including commercially, as long as you credit Damir Sokolovsky ([@heydamir](https://x.com/heydamir)) and link back to this repository.

picks.name: dsh-superagent-prototype
picks.desc: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System
picks.readme:
# dsh-superagent

> **Research prototype for reference only, not an official DeepSeek product.** This code grew out of our team's day-to-day development work, with much of the engineering done by coding agents. Treat it as research code, not production-ready software. It may still contain bugs, and its coding style and engineering practices may be inconsistent. Review and adapt it before using it in your own environment.
>
> We have adapted it for publication, so it is not identical to our internal version or the implementation described in *Exploring Super-agent Design: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System*. Some designs discussed in the article are directions for future development and are not implemented in this prototype.

dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged as a bundle for [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/en/harness/). It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. When someone allowed asks the agent for work, it opens a work item, works on it in its own agent session and directory, and answers in the original conversation, for example with a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person.

It is also a way of working with an agent: **take as little human attention as possible, and give as much value as possible.** An agent that can act for a whole team can also waste a whole team's attention, so it acts only when asked or when a rule the team wrote allows it, and speaks only when someone must act or can use a result. [docs/000-philosophy.md](docs/000-philosophy.md) explains the principle and what it asks of the operator.

## Setup

Setup has many steps, so an agent does it with you. Ask your coding agent:

> Read SETUP.md in this repository and set up dsh-superagent with me.

It asks one short question at a time, shows the full plan once, and then installs and configures everything. [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) is what it follows.

## Documentation

Read the numbered documents in order; each builds only on the ones before it.

- [000 Philosophy](docs/000-philosophy.md)
- [001 Domain model](docs/001-domain.md)
- [002 Authorization](docs/002-authorization.md)
- [003 Execution](docs/003-execution.md)
- [004 Prompts](docs/004-prompts.md)
- [005 Panel](docs/005-panel.md)
- [006 Deployment](docs/006-deployment.md): manual setup, configuration, upgrades and troubleshooting
- [007 Architecture](docs/007-architecture.md)
- [008 Cookbook](docs/008-cookbook.md): adding a Source

## Development

`pnpm check` runs the typecheck, the tests and the build.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

picks.name: agent-skills
picks.desc: Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents.
picks.readme:
# Agent Skills **Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents.** Skills encode the workflows, quality gates, and best practices that senior engineers use when building software. These ones are packaged so AI agents follow them consistently across every phase of development. ![Addy's Agent Skills](https://addyosmani.com/assets/images/addys-agent-skills.jpg) ``` DEFINE PLAN BUILD VERIFY REVIEW SHIP ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ │ Idea │ ───▶ │ Spec │ ───▶ │ Code │ ───▶ │ Test │ ───▶ │ QA │ ───▶ │ Go │ │Refine│ │ PRD │ │ Impl │ │Debug │ │ Gate │ │ Live │ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ /spec /plan /build /test /review /ship ``` --- ## Commands 9 slash commands that map to the development lifecycle. Each one activates the right skills automatically. | What you're doing | Command | Key principle | |-------------------|---------|---------------| | Define what to build | `/spec` | Spec before code | | Plan how to build it | `/plan` | Small, atomic tasks | | Build incrementally | `/build` | One slice at a time | | Prove it works | `/test` | Tests are proof | | Set the quality bar | `/constraints` | Decide it once, enforce it everywhere | | Review before merge | `/review` | Improve code health | | Audit web performance | `/webperf` | Measure before you optimize | | Simplify the code | `/code-simplify` | Clarity over cleverness | | Ship to production | `/ship` | Faster is safer | In Claude Code these install as plugin commands. Where a built-in command has the same name, as `/review` does, use the namespaced form: `/agent-skills:review`. Want fewer manual steps once the spec exists? **`/build auto`** generates the plan and implements every task in a single approved pass — you approve the plan once, then it runs autonomously. It removes the human stepping *between* tasks, not the verification: every task is still test-driven and committed individually, and it pauses on failures or risky steps. Skills also activate automatically based on what you're doing — designing an API triggers `api-and-interface-design`, building UI triggers `frontend-ui-engineering`, and so on. --- ## Quick Start **Fastest path — any agent, one command.** The open [skills CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) installs into 70+ agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Cline, and more): ```bash npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills # install all 25 skills npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --list # browse before installing ``` Or grab individual skills: ```bash npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --skill code-review-and-quality # five-axis review before merge npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --skill interview-me # requirements interrogation, one question at a time npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --skill test-driven-development # red-green-refactor, enforced ``` > **Installing one skill?** A per-skill `npx` install copies only > `skills//`, not the repo-level `references/` directory. The skill still > works, but paths to supplementary shared checklists are unavailable. Use a > whole-repo integration, clone the repository, or copy the needed checklist into > a `references/` directory inside the installed skill. This portability gap is > tracked in [#361](https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills/issues/361). Prefer a native integration? Pick your tool below.

picks.name: auto-ontology
picks.desc: Auto Ontology is a Python framework for building semantic, graph-based reasoning layers over data. It enables deterministic query generation, better context retrieval, and more explainable AI for LLM and agent workflows.
picks.readme:
# Auto Ontology Agents can retrieve documents and query databases, but reliability gates agentic analytics: a revenue metric answered faster is worth nothing if the number is wrong. Agents need a context layer that tells them where data lives, what it means, whether to use it, how to use it, where it came from, and what is similar. NVIDIA Auto Ontology is an open library that builds that layer from enterprise metadata, reconciles definitions across systems, and exposes it to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API. It complements the semantic models customers already own. It enables developers to: - Discover: generate enterprise ontologies from metadata; connect existing ontologies and semantic models; build AI-ready knowledge graphs. - Ground: give agents trusted business meaning for metrics, entities, and relationships; reconcile inconsistent definitions across systems. - Validate: check generated queries against certified definitions and lineage; return provenance with every answer. - Expose: serve context to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API. Learn: fold certified corrections and usage back into the ontology, so shared context improves with every question. ## Benchmarks To run a text-to-SQL benchmark such as BIRD, refer to the [ontology SQL evaluation repository](https://github.com/NVIDIA/ontology-sql-eval/). > **Licensing & contributions.** Auto Ontology is distributed under the > [Apache License 2.0](./LICENSE). Third-party open-source components > bundled, linked, or otherwise used by this project are listed in > [`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`](./THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). **This project > is currently not accepting external contributions.**

picks.desc: OpenAI's Codex Security CLI and TypeScript SDK for finding, validating, and fixing security vulnerabilities. npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@openai/codex-security
picks.readme:
# Codex Security

Codex Security helps you find, investigate, and fix vulnerabilities in your code.
Use its security workflows in Codex, or automate them with the
`@openai/codex-security` CLI and TypeScript SDK.

- **In Codex:** [choose a security workflow](docs/agent-workflows.md).
- **In a terminal:** [install the CLI and scan your repository](#quick-start).
- **In automation:** use the [TypeScript SDK](#typescript-sdk) or
  [GitHub Action](#github-actions).

## Features

- Scan repositories, selected paths, or Git changes. Deep scans repeat Standard scans and return their deduplicated findings.
- Validate candidate findings, generate patches, and verify existing fixes.
- Draft `SECURITY.md` policies and save threat models for later review.
- Browse saved scans and findings, identify duplicates, assess severity against
  your own rubric, and suggest owners from source and Git history.
- Preview third-party scanner findings, save them locally, or publish supported reports to Codex Security Cloud. [Scanner import guides](docs/scanner-imports/README.md).
- Track findings in Linear, Jira, or GitHub, publish completed scans, or export SARIF, JSON, and CSV. [Integration workflows](docs/plugin-connectors.md).
- Automate scans across repositories or project components, including in CI and
  containers.

## Use in Codex

Open your repository in a Codex session with the Codex Security plugin enabled,
then ask:

> Run a Codex Security scan on this repository, focusing on authentication and
> authorization. Return the saved report, source evidence, and coverage limits.

A completed scan saves a report and findings. Read the report for source
evidence and exclusions, then request a patch or ask Codex to verify an
existing fix. See the [agent workflow guide](docs/agent-workflows.md) for setup,
task selection, and recovery.

## Quick start

Requires Node.js 22.13.0+ within 22.x, or Node.js 24.x or 26.x, and Python 3.10+.
Python 3.10 also requires `tomli`.

Install the CLI globally and sign in:

```bash
npm install --global @openai/codex-security
cs login
```

Run your first scan from the repository directory:

```bash
cs scan .
```

When the scan completes, open the Markdown file at the **REPORT** path in the
terminal. Run `cs scans show` from the same repository to find its latest
completed scan again. See [scan scope and follow-up work](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#understand-scan-scope-and-follow-up-work)
for how to interpret exclusions in the report.

`cs` and `codex-security` run the same CLI. If the short name conflicts with
another command, use `codex-security`. To skip the global install, or if npm
reports an `EEXIST` conflict, use `npx @openai/codex-security` in place of
`cs` for both login and scanning.

For CI, set `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `CODEX_API_KEY` in the scan process's environment.
For a headless machine, see [device or SSH login](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#authentication).

### Scan options

Choose a scope and scan mode:

```bash
# Scan selected paths.
cs scan . --path src --path tests

# Scan committed changes from a base revision to HEAD.
cs scan . --diff origin/main

# Run a deep scan of the repository.
cs scan . --mode deep
```

Use `cs scan . --max-time 15` for an advisory 15-minute Standard investigation
allowance. See [investigation time](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#set-investigation-time)
for timing semantics and Deep Scan limits.

Use `cs --help` to browse commands, or `cs scan --help`
for scan options, cost limits, and patching after a scan.

For an application spread across repositories, see
[review one system across repositories](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#review-one-system-across-repositories).
Use [bulk scans](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#bulk-scans) for independent repository
reviews in one resumable campaign.

Scans use existing root and component `SECURITY.md` guidance. To write or
revise it, see [Generate SECURITY.md](#generate-securitymd).

picks.desc: Agent harness for learning difficult things.
picks.license_name: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0
picks.readme:
An agent harness for learning.

Download · How it works · Documentation · Issues · Discord

LearnHarness uses AI agents to plan and teach lessons from your current understanding to your goal. It builds a detailed picture of what you understand and how you reason. That picture is updated as you learn. Instead of just giving you an explanation, it uses your answers and thinking to decide what you need next. Teaching builds understanding one reasoning step at a time. Practice makes it usable. A persistent knowledge graph carries it across sessions. ![LearnHarness teaching session](docs/assets/teaching-session.png) ## How it works 1. **Measure.** Before teaching, the agent finds where your understanding ends on each part the lesson depends on. Your answers, confidence, and thinking show it where to start. 2. **Plan.** It works out a dependency map from that starting point to your goal. You can see the plan, and the lesson adapts when your understanding turns out different. 3. **Teach.** Each step builds on something you already understand. You predict, get an explanation, and check your understanding. Confusions are repaired before anything is built on them. The aim is for the goal to feel obviously true, not merely familiar. 4. **Practice.** Separate sessions pose varied problems that require the right knowledge to come to mind without being named first. Problems and hints adapt to your reasoning. **Think out loud.** The thinking fields let you explain your reasoning, uncertainties, and reactions in your own words. This is how the agent gets a detailed picture rather than just a record of right and wrong answers. You can type or use dictation. **Bring your files.** In the desktop app, attach PDFs, photos, or any other file with the paperclip, or drag them in. The file stays where it is: the message carries its path, and the agent reads it from there. The agent can also research questions in the background, create visual explanations, show your own images in the lesson and mark them up with arrows and labels, and build interactive demonstrations. ## Knowledge that carries forward What you are taught accumulates as propositions and reasoning chains: individual claims and the premises that lead to them. The graph shows this structure, with links back to the source sessions. You can also import notes. Future teaching sessions can read the graph instead of starting from scratch. Practice sessions can draw their material from it. It stores the ideas and their connections, not ratings of your ability. ![LearnHarness knowledge graph](docs/assets/knowledge-graph.png) ## Download and get started **[Download from learnharness.ai](https://learnharness.ai)** · [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/amosblomqvist/learnharness/releases) - **macOS (Apple Silicon):** signed and notarized DMG. Drag the app to Applications. - **Windows (x64):** run the installer. It is currently unsigned; Windows may show an “unknown publisher” or SmartScreen warning. - **Linux (x64):** make the AppImage executable and open it, or install the Debian/Ubuntu `.deb`. Choose your models, then start a session with what you want to understand. You can use provider API keys, supported subscription connections in the desktop app, an installed [Claude Code CLI](docs/claude-code.md), or a [custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint](docs/custom-providers.md), including a local model server.
